sense: of a computer, program or website

terms.grammar: present participle of ūtor, used as a noun
terms.comment: Our formation, the one the lexicon already uses in nōmen ūtentis (see username): no reference work has a word for a computer user. Classically the participle keeps its verb and takes the ablative (rēbus ūtentēs); as a noun it is clearest in the plural, ūtentēs, the people who use a program. Where a clause will do, Latin prefers the verb: quī hōc programmate ūtuntur, the users of this program.

phrases.english: How many users does this program have?

sources: Lewis & Short: utor
No reference work (Traupman, Morgan–Owens, Levi & Bini) has a word for a computer user.
